bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Ouyang Xiu

title.zh: 卷二十九 晉臣傳第十七: 桑維翰 景延廣 吳巒
title.en: Volume 29 Later Jin Biographies 9: Sang Weihan, Jing Yanguang, Wu Luan
title.raw: 卷二十九 晉臣傳第十七: 桑維翰 景延廣 吳巒 Volume 29 Later Jin Biographies 9: Sang Weihan, Jing Yanguang, Wu Luan

sentences.zh: 桑维翰

translations.literal: Sang Weihan
translations.idiomatic: Sang Weihan

sentences.zh: 桑维翰，字国侨，河南人也。

translations.literal: Sang Weihan, styled Guoqiao, was a native of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Weihan, styled Guoqiao, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 为人丑怪，身短而面长，常临鉴以自奇曰：「七尺之身，不如一尺之面。

translations.literal: His person was ugly and strange—short in stature and long in face. He often looked in a mirror and marveled at himself, saying: “A body of seven feet is not equal to a face of one foot.
translations.idiomatic: He was homely and odd—short-bodied, long-faced. He would study himself in a mirror and say: “Seven feet of body cannot match one foot of face.

sentences.zh: 」慨然有志于公辅。

translations.literal: ” He harbored a grand ambition for high office.
translations.idiomatic: ” He burned to reach the highest councils of state.

sentences.zh: 初举进士，主司恶其姓，以「桑」「丧」同音。

translations.literal: When he first took the jinshi examination, the chief examiner disliked his surname, because “Sang” and “mourning” were homophones.
translations.idiomatic: At his first jinshi attempt the chief examiner disliked his surname—“Sang” echoed “funeral.”

sentences.zh: 人有劝其不必举进士，可以从佗求仕者，维翰慨然，乃著《日出扶桑赋》以见志。

translations.literal: Someone urged him that he need not pursue the jinshi and could seek office by other paths. Weihan was indignant and wrote “Rising Sun over the Mulberry” to declare his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Friends said he need not sit the jinshi and could find office elsewhere. Weihan, stung, wrote “Rising Sun over the Mulberry” to show his resolve.

sentences.zh: 又铸铁砚以示人曰：「砚弊则改而佗仕。

translations.literal: He also cast an iron inkstone and told people: “When the stone wears out, I will change and seek another path.
translations.idiomatic: He cast an iron inkstone and said: “When this wears through, I change course—but not before.

sentences.zh: 」卒以进士及第。

translations.literal: ” In the end he passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: ” He passed the jinshi in the end.

sentences.zh: 晋高祖辟为河阳节度掌书记，其后常以自从。

translations.literal: The Jin High Ancestor made him chief secretary to the Heyang military governor, and afterward often kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin High Ancestor made him chief secretary at Heyang and kept him close thereafter.

sentences.zh: 高祖自太原徙天平，不受命，而有异谋，以问将佐，将佐皆恐惧不敢言，独维翰与刘知远赞成之，因使维翰为书求援于契丹。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor moved from Taiyuan to Tianping and refused orders, already harboring rebellion, he asked his officers. They were all afraid and dared not speak. Only Weihan and Liu Zhiyuan approved. He therefore had Weihan write seeking aid from the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor refused transfer from Taiyuan to Tianping and plotted rebellion. He asked his staff; all feared and were silent. Only Weihan and Liu Zhiyuan urged him on. Weihan wrote to the Khitan for aid.

sentences.zh: 耶律德光已许诺，而赵德钧亦以重赂啖德光，求助己以篡唐。

translations.literal: Yelü Deguang had already promised, but Zhao Dejun also bribed Deguang heavily, asking him to help seize Tang for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Deguang had promised—but Zhao Dejun bribed him to put himself on Tang’s throne instead.

sentences.zh: 高祖惧事不果，乃遣维翰往见德光，为陈利害甚辩，德光意乃决，卒以灭唐而兴晋，维翰之力也。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor feared the plan would fail and sent Weihan to see Deguang. He argued profit and harm with great eloquence; Deguang’s mind was settled. He at last destroyed Tang and raised Jin—Weihan’s power did this.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing failure, the High Ancestor sent Weihan to Deguang. Weihan argued the stakes so well that Deguang committed. Tang fell and Jin rose—chiefly through Weihan.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，以维翰为翰林学士、礼部侍郎、知枢密院事，迁中书侍郎、同中书门下平章事，兼枢密使。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne, Weihan was made Hanlin academician, Vice Minister of Rites, and director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then promoted to Vice Grand Councillor, co-signer of the Secretariat, and chief councillor of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At enthronement Weihan became Hanlin academician, Vice Minister of Rites, and Military Affairs director, then Vice Grand Councillor, co-signer, and chief councillor of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 天福四年，出为相州节度使，岁余，徙镇泰宁。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianfu he went out as military governor of Xiangzhou; after a year he was transferred to govern Taining.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu year four he governed Xiangzhou; a year later he moved to Taining.

sentences.zh: 吐浑白承福为契丹所迫，附镇州安重荣以归晋，重荣因请与契丹绝好，用吐浑以攻之。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun Bai Chengfu, pressed by the Khitan, attached himself to An Chongrong of Zhenzhou and submitted to Jin. Chongrong therefore asked to break with the Khitan and use the Tuyuhun to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Chengfu of the Tuyuhun, harried by the Khitan, joined An Chongrong at Zhen and submitted to Jin. Chongrong asked to break with the Khitan and strike them with Tuyuhun allies.

sentences.zh: 高祖重违重荣，意未决。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor was loath to oppose Chongrong and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor hesitated to cross Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 维翰上疏言契丹未可与争者七，高祖召维翰使者至卧内，谓曰：「北面之事，方挠吾胸中，得卿此疏，计已决矣，可无忧也。

translations.literal: Weihan memorialized seven reasons the Khitan could not be contested. The High Ancestor summoned Weihan’s messenger to his bedside and said: “The northern affair has been tangling my heart. With your master’s memorial the plan is settled—I need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan listed seven reasons not to fight the Khitan. The High Ancestor called the messenger to his bedside: “The north has tormented me. This memorial settles it.

sentences.zh: 」维翰又劝高祖幸邺都。

translations.literal: ” Weihan also urged the High Ancestor to visit the northern capital at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: ” Weihan also urged a royal progress to Ye.

sentences.zh: 七年，高祖在邺，维翰来朝，徙镇晋昌。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the High Ancestor was at Ye; Weihan came to court and was transferred to govern Jinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Year seven the High Ancestor was at Ye. Weihan attended court and was sent to Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 出帝即位，召拜侍中。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Weihan was summoned and made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor made him Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 而景延广用事，与契丹绝盟，维翰言不能入，乃阴使人说帝曰：「制契丹而安天下，非用维翰不可。

translations.literal: Jing Yanguang held power and broke the Khitan alliance. Weihan’s counsel could not enter. He secretly had men tell the emperor: “To control the Khitan and secure the realm, none but Weihan will do.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang ruled and broke the Khitan pact. Weihan’s voice was shut out. He secretly urged the throne: “Only Weihan can tame the Khitan and steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 」乃出延广于河南，拜维翰中书令，复为枢密使，封魏国公，事无巨细，一以委之。

translations.literal: ” Yanguang was sent out to govern Henan; Weihan was made Grand Secretary and again chief councillor of Military Affairs, enfeoffed Duke of Wei. Great and small affairs were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yanguang went to Henan; Weihan became Grand Secretary and Military Affairs chief, Duke of Wei. Every matter passed through his hands.

sentences.zh: 数月之间，百度浸理。

translations.literal: Within months the hundred offices were gradually set in order.
translations.idiomatic: Within months government found its rhythm again.

sentences.zh: 初，李瀚为翰林学士，好饮而多酒过，高祖以为浮薄。

translations.literal: At first Li Han was Hanlin academician, fond of drink and often drunk. The High Ancestor thought him frivolous.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han of the Hanlin loved wine and drank too deep. The High Ancestor found him flighty.

sentences.zh: 天福五年九月，诏废翰林学士，按《唐六典》归其职于中书舍人，而端明殿学士、枢密院学士皆废。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Tianfu’s fifth year an edict abolished Hanlin academicians and, per the Tang Six Offices canon, returned their duties to Secretariat drafters; Duanming academics and Military Affairs academics were also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu five, ninth month: Hanlin posts were abolished and their work returned to Secretariat drafters; Duanming and Military Affairs academics went too.

sentences.zh: 及维翰为枢密使，复奏置学士，而悉用亲旧为之。

translations.literal: When Weihan became chief councillor of Military Affairs he memorialized to restore academics—and filled every seat with kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: As Military Affairs chief Weihan restored the academics—and stocked them with kin and cronies.

sentences.zh: 维翰权势既盛，四方赂遗，岁积巨万。

translations.literal: Weihan’s power grew vast; gifts from the four directions piled to tens of thousands each year.
translations.idiomatic: His power swelled; bribes from every quarter piled into the tens of thousands yearly.

sentences.zh: 内客省使李彦韬、端明殿学士冯玉用事，共谗之。

translations.literal: The Inner Service commissioner Li Yantao and Duanming academician Feng Yu held sway and slandered him together.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yantao of the Inner Service and Feng Yu of Duanming ruled the whispering gallery against him.

sentences.zh: 帝欲骤黜维翰，大臣刘昫、李崧皆以为不可，卒以玉为枢密使，既而以为相，维翰日益见疏。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to dismiss Weihan abruptly. Ministers Liu Xu and Li Song said it could not be done. Feng Yu was made Military Affairs chief and soon chief councillor; Weihan was daily more estranged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to oust Weihan at once. Liu Xu and Li Song forbade it. Feng Yu took Military Affairs, then the chief councillor’s seat; Weihan faded.

sentences.zh: 帝饮酒过度得疾，维翰遣人阴白太后，请为皇弟重睿置师傅。

translations.literal: The emperor drank to excess and fell ill. Weihan secretly informed the empress dowager to appoint tutors for the imperial younger brother Chongrui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drank himself ill. Weihan secretly told the empress dowager to name tutors for Prince Chongrui.

sentences.zh: 帝疾愈，知之，怒，乃罢维翰以为开封尹。

translations.literal: When the emperor recovered he learned of it and was angry. He demoted Weihan to mayor of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Recovered, he learned of the plot and in rage made Weihan mayor of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 维翰遂称足疾，稀复朝见。

translations.literal: Weihan then claimed foot ailment and seldom attended court.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan pleaded bad feet and rarely came to court.

sentences.zh: 契丹屯中渡，破栾城，杜重威等大军隔绝，维翰曰：「事急矣！

translations.literal: The Khitan encamped at Zhongdu Ferry and broke Luan City; Du Chongwei’s great army was cut off. Weihan said: “The affair is desperate!
translations.idiomatic: Khitan troops held Zhongdu Ferry and took Luan City; Du Chongwei’s host was severed. Weihan said: “We are at the brink!

sentences.zh: 」乃见冯玉等计事，而谋不合。

translations.literal: ” He went to Feng Yu and the others to plan, but their counsel did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sought Feng Yu and the rest—but they would not agree.

sentences.zh: 又求见帝，帝方调鹰于苑中，不暇见，维翰退而叹曰：「晋不血食矣！」

translations.literal: He asked audience again; the emperor was training hawks in the park and had no time. Weihan withdrew and sighed: “Jin will offer no blood at the altars!
translations.idiomatic: He begged audience; the emperor was flying hawks in the park. Weihan withdrew: “Jin’s altars will run dry!

sentences.zh: 自契丹与晋盟，始成于维翰，而终败于景延广，故自兵兴，契丹凡所书檄，未尝不以此两人为言。

translations.literal: From the Khitan alliance with Jin—first sealed by Weihan, finally broken by Yanguang—once war began, every Khitan proclamation named these two men.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan pact with Jin began with Weihan and ended with Yanguang; once war came, every Khitan letter named them both.

sentences.zh: 耶律德光犯京师，遣张彦泽遗太后书，问此两人在否，可使先来。

translations.literal: Yelü Deguang entered the capital and sent Zhang Yanzhe with a letter to the empress dowager, asking whether these two were still alive and could come first.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang reached the capital and sent Zhang Yanzhe to the empress dowager: were they alive? Send them first.

sentences.zh: 而帝以继翰尝议毋绝盟而己违之也，不欲使维翰见德光，因讽彦泽图之，而彦泽亦利其赀产。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Jihan had once urged never breaking the alliance and he himself had violated it, did not wish Weihan to see Deguang. He hinted Yanzhe should deal with him—and Yanzhe coveted his wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had ignored Weihan’s counsel to keep the pact and did not want him before Deguang. He nudged Yanzhe—and Yanzhe wanted his estate.

sentences.zh: 维翰状貌既异，素以威严自持，晋之老将大臣，见者无不屈服，彦泽以骁捍自矜，每往候之，虽冬月未尝不流汗。

translations.literal: Weihan’s appearance was already strange and he always held himself with stern dignity. Jin’s old generals and great ministers all bowed before him. Yanzhe was proud of his fierceness, yet each visit left him sweating even in winter.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan looked uncanny and ruled by sheer presence; Jin’s veterans bowed low. Yanzhe, swaggering in his brutality, sweated through winter visits.

sentences.zh: 初，彦泽入京师，左右劝维翰避祸，维翰曰：「吾为大臣，国家至此，安所逃死邪！

translations.literal: When Yanzhe first entered the capital, his attendants urged Weihan to flee disaster. Weihan said: “I am a great minister. The state has come to this—where would I flee death?
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhe entered the capital; aides urged flight. Weihan said: “I am a great minister. The realm is fallen—where would I hide?

sentences.zh: 」安坐府中不动。

translations.literal: ” He sat in his office unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sat still in his yamen.

sentences.zh: 彦泽以兵入，问：「维翰何在？

translations.literal: Yanzhe entered with troops and asked: “Where is Weihan?
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhe marched in: “Where is Weihan?

sentences.zh: 」维翰厉声曰：「吾，晋大臣，自当死国，安得无礼邪！

translations.literal: ” Weihan cried in a harsh voice: “I am a Jin great minister. I should die for the state—how dare you be rude!
translations.idiomatic: ” Weihan’s voice cracked like iron: “I am Jin’s minister. I die for the state—show respect!

sentences.zh: 」彦泽股栗不敢仰视，退而谓人曰：「吾不知桑维翰何如人，今日见之，犹使人恐惧如此，其可再见乎？

translations.literal: ” Yanzhe’s legs trembled; he dared not look up. He withdrew and told others: “I did not know what sort of man Sang Weihan was. To see him today still inspires such fear—how could I see him again?
translations.idiomatic: ” Yanzhe’s knees buckled; he could not meet his eyes. Outside he said: “Who knew Sang Weihan was such a man? Once was enough—I could not face him twice.

sentences.zh: 」乃以帝命召维翰。

translations.literal: ” He then summoned Weihan by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: ” Then he summoned Weihan in the emperor’s name.

sentences.zh: 维翰行，遇李崧，立马而语，军吏前白维翰，请赴侍卫司狱。

translations.literal: Weihan went out and met Li Song; they spoke halting their horses. An officer came forward and told Weihan to go to the Guard Bureau prison.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan met Li Song on the road and spoke from horseback. An officer said he was bound for the Guard Bureau prison.

sentences.zh: 维翰知不免，顾崧曰：「相公当国，使维翰独死？

translations.literal: Knowing he could not escape, Weihan turned to Song and said: “You held the state—must Weihan die alone?
translations.idiomatic: Weihan knew the end. He said to Song: “You ran the realm—must I die alone?

sentences.zh: 」崧惭不能对。

translations.literal: ” Song was ashamed and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: ” Song flushed and was silent.

sentences.zh: 是夜，彦泽使人缢杀之，以帛加颈，告德光曰：「维翰自缢。

translations.literal: That night Yanzhe had a man strangle him with silk about the neck and told Deguang: “Weihan hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yanzhe had him strangled with silk and reported: “Weihan took his own life.

sentences.zh: 」德光曰：「我本无心杀维翰，维翰何必自致。

translations.literal: ” Deguang said: “I had no heart to kill Weihan—why did he bring it on himself?
translations.idiomatic: ” Deguang said: “I never meant to kill him—why force my hand?

sentences.zh: 」德光至京师，使人检其尸，信为缢死，乃以尸赐其家，而赀财悉为彦泽所掠。

translations.literal: ” When Deguang reached the capital he had the corpse examined; seeing it was truly strangulation, he returned the body to the family—but all wealth was plundered by Yanzhe.
translations.idiomatic: ” At the capital he inspected the body, accepted the story, and returned it to kin—but Yanzhe had stripped the estate bare.

sentences.zh: 景延广

translations.literal: Jing Yanguang
translations.idiomatic: Jing Yanguang

sentences.zh: 景延广，字航川，陕州人也。

translations.literal: Jing Yanguang, styled Hangchuan, was a native of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Yanguang, styled Hangchuan, came from Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父建善射，尝教延广曰：「射不入铁，不如不发。

translations.literal: His father Jian was skilled at archery and once taught Yanguang: “If the shot does not pierce iron, better not to loose.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian was a master bowman and taught him: “If you cannot pierce iron, do not shoot.

sentences.zh: 」由是延广以挽强见称。

translations.literal: ” From this Yanguang was famed for drawing the heavy bow.
translations.idiomatic: ” He became famous for the heavy bow.

sentences.zh: 事梁邵王友诲，友诲谋反被幽，延广亡去。

translations.literal: He served Liang’s Prince of Shao Youhai; when Youhai rebelled and was imprisoned, Yanguang fled.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liang’s Prince of Shao Youhai; when Youhai rebelled and was jailed, Yanguang fled.

sentences.zh: 后从王彦章战中都，彦章败，延广身被数创，仅以身免。

translations.literal: Later he followed Wang Yanzhang in battle at Zhongdu; Yanzhang was defeated and Yanguang took many wounds, barely escaping with his life.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wang Yanzhang at Zhongdu; Yanzhang fell and Yanguang was riddled with wounds, barely alive.

sentences.zh: 明宗时，朱守殷以汴州反，晋高祖为六军副使，主诛从守殷反者。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong, Zhu Shouyin rebelled at Bianzhou. The Jin High Ancestor was deputy commander of the Six Armies and oversaw executing Shouyin’s followers.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong, Zhu Shouyin rebelled at Bian. The Jin High Ancestor commanded punishment of the rebels.

sentences.zh: 延广为汴州军校当诛，高祖惜其才，阴纵之使亡，后录以为客将。

translations.literal: Yanguang was a Bianzhou officer due for execution. The High Ancestor prized his talent and secretly let him escape; later he enrolled him as a guest officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang was marked for death. The High Ancestor prized him, let him slip away, and later took him as a guest officer.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，以为侍卫步军都指挥使，领果州团练使，从领宁江军节度使。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne, Yanguang was made commander of the palace foot guard and concurrent regimental commissioner of Guozhou, then military governor of Ningjiang.
translations.idiomatic: At enthronement Yanguang commanded the palace foot guard and governed Guo, then Ningjiang.

sentences.zh: 天福四年，出镇义成，又徙保义，复召为侍卫马步军都虞候，徙镇河阳三城，迁马步军都指挥使，领天平。

translations.literal: In Tianfu’s fourth year he went out to govern Yicheng, then was moved to Baoyi, recalled as deputy commander of palace horse and foot, transferred to the three cities of Heyang, promoted to commander of horse and foot, and given Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu four he held Yicheng, then Baoyi; he returned as deputy commander of horse and foot, held Heyang’s three cities, then Tianping.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，出帝立，延广有力，颇伐其功。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor died and the Deposed Emperor rose, Yanguang had leverage and boasted of his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor died; the Deposed Emperor rose. Yanguang had clout and trumpeted his deeds.

sentences.zh: 初，出帝立，晋大臣议告契丹，致表称臣，延广独不肯，但致书称孙而已，大臣皆知其不可而不能夺。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor first took the throne, Jin’s ministers debated notifying the Khitan with a memorial of subjection. Yanguang alone refused—he sent only a letter calling himself grandson. The ministers all knew it would not do but could not overrule him.
translations.idiomatic: At the new reign Jin’s ministers meant to notify the Khitan as subjects. Yanguang alone refused—he wrote as grandson, not vassal. Everyone knew disaster would follow; none could stop him.

sentences.zh: 契丹果怒，数以责晋，延广谓契丹使者乔莹曰：「先皇帝北朝所立，今卫子中国自册，可以为孙，而不可为臣。

translations.literal: The Khitan were enraged and repeatedly reproached Jin. Yanguang told the Khitan envoy Qiao Ying: “The former emperor was enthroned by your court. Now the Son of Heaven of Weizi enthrones himself—we may be grandson, but not subject.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan raged and rebuked Jin again and again. Yanguang told envoy Qiao Ying: “Your court made our last emperor. Weizi’s Son of Heaven enthrones himself—we are grandson, not subject.

sentences.zh: 且晋有横磨大剑十万口，翁要战则来，佗日不禁孙子，取笑天下。

translations.literal: Moreover Jin has a hundred thousand horizontal-grinding great swords. If the old man wants war, let him come. Another day he may not restrain his grandson—the realm will laugh.
translations.idiomatic: Jin keeps a hundred thousand “horizontal-grinding” great swords. If you want war, come. One day you may fail to leash your grandson—and the world will laugh.

sentences.zh: 」莹知其言必起两国之争，惧后无以取信也，因请载于纸，以备遗忘。

translations.literal: Ying knew these words would surely raise strife between the two states and feared he could not be believed later. He asked that they be written down lest he forget.
translations.idiomatic: Ying knew this would kindle war and feared he would not be believed. He asked for it in writing.

sentences.zh: 延广敕吏具载以授莹，莹藏其书衣领中以归，具以延广语告契丹，契丹益怒。

translations.literal: Yanguang ordered a clerk to record and give it to Ying. Ying hid the paper in his collar and returned, reporting Yanguang’s words in full. The Khitan grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang had it written and handed over. Ying hid it in his collar, repeated every word at home, and the Khitan fury doubled.

sentences.zh: 天福八年秋，出帝幸大年庄还，置酒延广第。

translations.literal: In the autumn of Tianfu’s eighth year the Deposed Emperor visited Danian Manor on his return and held wine at Yanguang’s house.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, Tianfu eight: the emperor feasted at Yanguang’s house after Danian Manor.

sentences.zh: 延广所进器服、鞍马、茶床、椅榻皆裹金银，饰以龙凤。

translations.literal: The vessels, saddles, tea tables, and couches Yanguang presented were all wrapped in gold and silver and ornamented with dragon and phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: His gifts—vessels, saddles, tea tables, couches—were sheathed in gold and silver, dragon- and phoenix-trimmed.

sentences.zh: 又进帛五千匹，绵一千四百两，马二十二匹，玉鞍、衣袭、犀玉、金带等，请赐从官，自皇弟重睿，下至伴食刺史、重睿从者各有差。

translations.literal: He also presented five thousand bolts of silk, fourteen hundred catties of cotton, twenty-two horses, jade saddles, robes, rhinoceros and jade, gold belts, and the like, asking that they be given to the entourage—from Prince Chongrui down to attendant prefects and Chongrui’s followers, each in due measure.
translations.idiomatic: He added five thousand bolts of silk, fourteen hundred catties of cotton, twenty-two horses, jade gear and gold belts for the court—from Chongrui to the humblest attendant, each by rank.

sentences.zh: 帝亦赐延广及其母、妻、从事、押衙、孔目官等称是。

translations.literal: The emperor also rewarded Yanguang, his mother, wife, staff, chief clerk, and accountants in kind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor matched gifts to Yanguang’s household and staff.

sentences.zh: 时天下旱、蝗，民饿死者岁十数万，而君臣穷极奢侈以相夸尚如此。

translations.literal: The realm suffered drought and locusts; hundreds of thousands starved each year—yet ruler and ministers flaunted luxury to outdo one another thus.
translations.idiomatic: Drought and locusts killed hundreds of thousands yearly—yet court and emperor competed in waste.

sentences.zh: 明年春，契丹入寇，延广从出帝北征为御营使，相拒澶、魏之间。

translations.literal: The next spring the Khitan invaded. Yanguang followed the Deposed Emperor north as commissioner of the imperial camp, facing them between Chan and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring the Khitan invaded. Yanguang marched north as imperial camp commissioner, facing them between Chan and Wei.

sentences.zh: 先锋石公霸遇虏于戚城，高行周、符彦卿兵少不能救，驰骑促延广益兵，延广按兵不动。

translations.literal: The vanguard Shi Gongba met the enemy at Weicheng. Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing had too few men to save him and sent riders urging Yanguang for more troops. Yanguang held his army still.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard Shi Gongba met the enemy at Weicheng. Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing could not break through and begged Yanguang for troops. He would not move.

sentences.zh: 三将被围数重，帝自御军救之，三将得出，皆泣诉。

translations.literal: The three generals were surrounded many ranks deep. The emperor led the army himself to rescue them; the three got out and wept their grievances.
translations.idiomatic: The three were ringed many deep. The emperor rode to save them; they emerged weeping.

sentences.zh: 然延广方握亲兵，恃功恣横，诸将皆由其节度，帝亦不能制也。

translations.literal: Yet Yanguang held the personal guard, trusting in merit and acting wantonly. Every general was under his command, and the emperor could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang held the imperial guard, arrogant with merit. Every general answered to him; the emperor could not check him.

sentences.zh: 契丹尝呼晋人曰：「景延广唤我来，何不速战？

translations.literal: The Khitan would call to the Jin men: “Jing Yanguang summoned me—why not fight at once?
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan shouted at Jin troops: “Yanguang called us—why delay the fight?

sentences.zh: 」是时，诸将皆力战，而延广未尝见敌。

translations.literal: ” At that time every general fought hard, but Yanguang never met the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: ” Others fought; Yanguang never faced the foe.

sentences.zh: 契丹已去，延广独闭壁不敢出。

translations.literal: After the Khitan withdrew, Yanguang alone shut his walls and dared not go out.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan left, Yanguang alone barred his gates.

sentences.zh: 自延广一言而契丹与晋交恶，凡号令征伐一出延广，晋大臣皆不得与，故契丹凡所书檄，未尝不以延广为言。

translations.literal: From Yanguang’s one speech Jin and the Khitan turned enemies. Every order and campaign came from Yanguang alone; Jin’s great ministers had no part. Thus every Khitan proclamation named Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: One speech from Yanguang poisoned Jin and Khitan. Orders and campaigns were his alone; ministers had no share. Every Khitan letter named him.

sentences.zh: 契丹去，出帝还京师，乃出延广为河南尹，留守西京。

translations.literal: When the Khitan left, the Deposed Emperor returned to the capital and sent Yanguang out as mayor of Henan, regent of the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan withdrew; the emperor sent Yanguang to govern Henan and hold the western capital.

sentences.zh: 明年，出帝幸澶渊，以延广从，皆无功。

translations.literal: The next year the Deposed Emperor visited Chanyuan with Yanguang—without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he marched to Chanyuan with Yanguang—to no gain.

sentences.zh: 延广居洛阳，郁郁不得志。

translations.literal: Yanguang lived in Luoyang, depressed and unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang he brooded, thwarted.

sentences.zh: 见晋日削，度必不能支契丹，乃为长夜之饮，大治第宅，园置妓乐，惟意所为。

translations.literal: Seeing Jin daily weaken and judging it could not stand against the Khitan, he gave himself to all-night drinking, built a great mansion, stocked gardens with singers and players, and did as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jin crumbled daily; he knew it could not hold. He drank through the nights, built a palace, filled gardens with music, and indulged every whim.

sentences.zh: 后帝亦追悔，遣供奉官张晖奉表称臣以求和，德光报曰：「使桑维翰、景延广来，而割镇、定与我，乃可和。

translations.literal: Later the emperor also repented and sent the attendant Zhang Hui with a memorial of subjection seeking peace. Deguang replied: “Send Sang Weihan and Jing Yanguang, and cede Zhen and Ding to me—then there may be peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repented and sent Zhang Hui to submit. Deguang answered: “Send Weihan and Yanguang; cede Zhen and Ding—then peace.

sentences.zh: 」晋知其不可，乃止。

translations.literal: ” Jin knew it could not be and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jin knew it was impossible and desisted.

sentences.zh: 契丹至中渡，延广屯河阳，闻杜重威降，乃还。

translations.literal: When the Khitan reached Zhongdu Ferry, Yanguang held Heyang. Hearing Du Chongwei had surrendered, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan troops reached Zhongdu Ferry. Yanguang held Heyang, heard Chongwei had surrendered, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 德光犯京师，行至相州，遣骑兵数千杂晋军渡河趋洛，以取延广，戒曰：「延广南奔吴，西走蜀，必追而取之。

translations.literal: Deguang entered the capital. Reaching Xiangzhou he sent several thousand cavalry mixed with Jin troops across the river toward Luoyang to seize Yanguang, warning: “If Yanguang flees south to Wu or west to Shu, pursue and take him.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang marched on the capital. At Xiangzhou he sent thousands of horse with Jin units toward Luoyang for Yanguang: “If he flees to Wu or Shu, take him.

sentences.zh: 」而延广顾虑其家，未能引决，虏骑奄至，乃与从事阎丕驰骑见德光于封丘，并丕见锁。

translations.literal: ” Yanguang, thinking of his family, could not resolve to die. Khitan riders suddenly arrived. He and his aide Yan Pi rode to see Deguang at Fengqiu; Pi was bound as well.
translations.idiomatic: ” He could not leave his family. Khitan horse swept in. He and aide Yan Pi rode to Deguang at Fengqiu; Pi was chained too.

sentences.zh: 延广曰：「丕，臣从事也，以职相随，何罪而见锁？

translations.literal: Yanguang said: “Pi is my staff officer and followed by duty—what crime warrants chains?
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang said: “Pi serves by duty—why chain him?

sentences.zh: 」丕乃得释。

translations.literal: ” Pi was then released.
translations.idiomatic: ” Pi was freed.

sentences.zh: 德光责延广曰：「南北失欢，皆因尔也。

translations.literal: Deguang reproached Yanguang: “North and south lost harmony—all because of you.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang rebuked him: “You broke north and south.

sentences.zh: 」召乔莹质其前言，延广初不服，莹从衣领中出所藏书，延广乃服。

translations.literal: ” He summoned Qiao Ying to verify the earlier words. Yanguang at first denied; Ying drew the hidden paper from his collar. Yanguang then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: ” He called Qiao Ying. Yanguang denied until Ying produced the paper from his collar. Then he yielded.

sentences.zh: 因以十事责延广，每服一事，授一牙筹，授至八筹，延广以面伏地，不能仰视，遂叱而锁之。

translations.literal: Deguang then charged him with ten counts; for each admission he gave one tally stick. At eight sticks Yanguang lay face down and could not look up. He was shouted at and bound.
translations.idiomatic: Ten charges, one tally each confession. At eight Yanguang lay facedown, unable to look up. They bound him.

sentences.zh: 将送之北行，至陈桥，止民家。

translations.literal: About to send him north, at Chen Bridge they stopped at a commoner’s house.
translations.idiomatic: They were sending him north; at Chen Bridge he lodged in a common house.

sentences.zh: 夜分，延广伺守者殆，引手扼吭而死，时年五十六。

translations.literal: Deep in the night, when the guards slackened, Yanguang reached up and throttled himself to death. He was fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: At night, guards slack, he seized his throat and died. He was fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 汉高祖时，赠侍中。

translations.literal: Under the Han High Ancestor he was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han posthumously made him Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 呜呼，自古祸福成败之理，未有如晋氏之明验也！

translations.literal: Alas—the principle of fortune, disaster, success, and failure has never been so clearly shown as in the house of Jin!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—fortune and ruin never proved themselves so plainly as in Jin!

sentences.zh: 其始以契丹而兴，终为契丹所灭。

translations.literal: They rose through the Khitan and in the end were destroyed by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: They rose by the Khitan and fell by the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 然方其以逆抗顺，大事未集，孤城被围，外无救援，而徒将一介之命，持片舌之强，能使契丹空国兴师，应若符契，出危解难，遂成晋氏，当是之时，维翰之力为多。

translations.literal: Yet when they opposed the mandate with rebellion, the great affair unfinished, a lone city besieged without relief from outside, and with only one man’s life and a tongue’s bravado could move the Khitan to empty the realm and march—answering like a tally, lifting peril and difficulty, and so establishing Jin—at that time Weihan’s power was the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the days of rebellion—besieged, unreinforced, with one life and one tongue—Weihan moved the Khitan to march as if by covenant, pulled Jin through, and built the dynasty. Then his was the greater share.

sentences.zh: 及少主新立，衅结兵连，败约起争，发自延广。

translations.literal: When the Young Lord newly took the throne, enmity tied itself to war, the broken pact and rising quarrel began from Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: The Young Lord’s reign tied enmity to war; the broken pact began with Yanguang.

sentences.zh: 然则晋氏之事，维翰成之，延广坏之，二人之用心者异，而其受祸也同，其故何哉？

translations.literal: Thus in Jin’s affairs Weihan accomplished them and Yanguang ruined them. The two men’s hearts differed, yet they suffered the same disaster. Why?
translations.idiomatic: Jin rose by Weihan and broke by Yanguang—different hearts, the same ruin. Why?

sentences.zh: 盖夫本末不顺而与夷狄共事者，常见其祸，未见其福也。

translations.literal: When root and branch are out of order and one works with barbarians, one often sees disaster and seldom sees blessing.
translations.idiomatic: When order is upside down and you lean on barbarians, you see ruin far more often than reward.

sentences.zh: 可不戒哉！

translations.literal: Is it not a warning!
translations.idiomatic: Take warning!

sentences.zh: 可不戒哉！

translations.literal: Is it not a warning!
translations.idiomatic: Take warning again!

sentences.zh: 吴峦，字宝川，郓州卢县人也。

translations.literal: Wu Luan, styled Baochuan, was a native of Lu County in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Luan, styled Baochuan, came from Lu County in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少举明经不中，清泰中为大同沙彦珣节度判官。

translations.literal: In youth he took the Mingjing examination but did not pass. In the Qingtai era he was chief secretary to Sha Yanxun, military governor of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the Mingjing in youth. Under Qingtai he was chief secretary to Sha Yanxun of Datong.

sentences.zh: 晋高祖起太原，召契丹为援，契丹过云州，彦珣出城迎谒，为契丹所虏。

translations.literal: When the Jin High Ancestor rose at Taiyuan and called the Khitan as allies, the Khitan passed Yun Prefecture. Yanxun went out to welcome them and was taken by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin High Ancestor rose at Taiyuan and called in the Khitan. They passed Yun; Yanxun went out to greet them and was captured.

sentences.zh: 城中推峦主州事，峦即闭门拒守，契丹以兵围之。

translations.literal: The city pushed Luan to manage affairs. Luan shut the gates and refused to yield. The Khitan besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: The city made Luan governor. He shut the gates and held. The Khitan besieged him.

sentences.zh: 高祖入立，以云州入于契丹，而峦犹守城不下，契丹围之凡七月。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne he ceded Yun Prefecture to the Khitan, yet Luan still held the city and would not come down. The Khitan besieged it for seven months in all.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor ceded Yun to the Khitan—but Luan still would not yield. The siege lasted seven months.

sentences.zh: 高祖义峦所为，乃以书告契丹，使解兵去。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor honored Luan’s conduct and wrote the Khitan asking them to lift the siege.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor admired his stand and asked the Khitan to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 高祖召峦，以为武宁军节度副使、谏议大夫、复州防御使。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor summoned Luan and made him deputy military governor of Wuning, Remonstrating Censor, and defender of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Luan, made him deputy governor of Wuning, Remonstrating Censor, and defender of Fu.

sentences.zh: 出帝即位，与契丹绝盟，河北诸州皆警，以谓贝州水陆之冲，缓急可以转饷，乃积刍粟数十万，以王令温为永清军节度使。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne and broke with the Khitan, every prefecture north of the river was alarmed. Beizhou was held the crossroads of land and water—grain could be shifted there in emergency. They stored hundreds of thousands of bundles of fodder and made Wang Lingwen military governor of the Yongqing army.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor broke with the Khitan; the north was on edge. Beizhou sat on land and water routes—fodder could be rushed there in crisis. They piled hundreds of thousands of bundles and made Wang Lingwen governor of Yongqing.

sentences.zh: 令温牙将邵珂，素骄很难制，令温夺其职。

translations.literal: Lingwen’s adjutant Shao Ke was by nature arrogant and hard to control. Lingwen stripped him of his post.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Shao Ke was proud and ungovernable. Lingwen removed him.

sentences.zh: 珂闲居无憀，乃阴使人亡入契丹，言贝州积粟多而无兵守，可取。

translations.literal: Ke, idle and bored, secretly sent men to flee into the Khitan and said Beizhou had much stored grain and few defenders—it could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Idle and bitter, Ke sent word to the Khitan: Beizhou was full of grain and bare of troops—ripe for the taking.

sentences.zh: 令温以事朝京师，心颇疑珂，乃质其子崇范以自随。

translations.literal: Lingwen went to court on business and suspected Ke; he took his son Chongfan as hostage on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwen went to court, uneasy about Ke, and brought his son Chongfan as surety.

sentences.zh: 晋大臣以峦前守云州七月，契丹不能下，乃遣峦驰驿代令温守贝州。

translations.literal: Jin’s great ministers, because Luan had once held Yun for seven months while the Khitan could not take it, sent Luan by relay to replace Lingwen and hold Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers remembered Luan’s seven months at Yun; they sent him by relay to replace Lingwen at Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 峦善抚士卒，会天大寒，裂其帷幄以衣士卒，士卒皆爱之。

translations.literal: Luan treated the troops well. It happened to be bitter cold; he tore his curtains and tents to clothe the soldiers, and they loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Luan cared for his men. In bitter cold he ripped curtains and tents for their coats; they loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 珂因求见蛮，愿自效，峦推心信之。

translations.literal: Ke then asked to see Luan and offered his service. Luan trusted him openly.
translations.idiomatic: Ke asked audience and pledged loyalty. Luan took him at his word.

sentences.zh: 开运元年正月，契丹南寇，围贝州，峦命珂守南门。

translations.literal: In the first month of Kaiyun’s first year the Khitan raided south and besieged Beizhou. Luan ordered Ke to hold the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyun 1, first month: the Khitan besieged Beizhou. Luan put Ke on the south gate.

sentences.zh: 契丹围三日，四面急攻之，峦从城上投薪草焚其梯冲殆尽。

translations.literal: After three days of assault on every side, Luan from the wall threw fuel and straw and burned their ladders and rams nearly clean.
translations.idiomatic: Three days they assaulted every wall. Luan hurled fuel and straw and burned ladders and rams to ash.

sentences.zh: 已而珂自南门引契丹入，峦守东门方战，而左右报珂反，峦顾城中已乱，即投井死。

translations.literal: Then Ke opened the south gate and led the Khitan in. Luan was fighting at the east gate when his men reported Ke’s treason. Seeing the city already in chaos, he threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Ke opened the south gate to the Khitan. Luan fought at the east until word came of treason. The city was lost; he threw himself into a well.

sentences.zh: 而令温家属为契丹所虏，出帝悯之，以令温为武胜军节度使，后累历方镇，周显德中卒。

translations.literal: Lingwen’s family was taken by the Khitan. The Deposed Emperor pitied him and made Lingwen military governor of Wusheng; later he served several commands and died in the Xiande era of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwen’s family was captured. The emperor pitied him and made him governor of Wusheng; he served on until Zhou’s Xiande era.

sentences.zh: 令温，瀛州河间人也。

translations.literal: Lingwen was a native of Hejian in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwen came from Hejian in Ying Prefecture.
